description:
lib.rs:312 — The default method check_revocation_against_anchor() returns crate::Result<()> but has no # Errors section. clippy::missing_errors_doc (pedantic) flags this.

The default always returns Ok(()), so the correct fix is a # Errors section noting:
'The default implementation always returns Ok(()) and never errors. Overriding implementations should document their own error conditions.'

This is documentation completeness, not a behaviour change.
title: [rusty/pkix-revocation] add # Errors to RevocationChecker::check_revocation_against_anchor default
